data.text: In a small internal exercise, six office volunteers compared three layouts: a table, a chart, and a paragraph summary. Each saw the same invented sample figures and answered two kinds of questions: one about an exact value and one about changes across the sequence. Participants found the table easiest to scan for exact values, while the chart helped them notice broad changes. The summary prompted useful discussion, though several volunteers went back to the table to confirm a number. We took notes, not completion times, so we cannot say any layout was faster. The figures did not represent a live service, and this small office group cannot tell us what all readers would prefer. These observations can guide the next prototype. A further round could include people who do not work with these figures every day and ask how they reached their answers to see whether the apparent preference holds beyond this group.
changes: Tightened the findings and kept the study limits and next step.

data.text: The cache expires each entry 30 minutes after the last successful fetch. Requests made before expiry return the stored value, even if the source has changed. Returning that value does not restart the 30-minute period; only a successful fetch does. After expiry, the next request attempts a fresh fetch. If it succeeds, the service stores the new value and starts a new expiry period. If it fails, the service returns an error, not the expired value. This matters on the settings page, where an old value could suggest a recent change had already taken effect. The prototype does not retry a failed fetch in the background. A later request can try again, and a successful attempt restores the normal cached path. These rules apply to the current prototype and may change after load testing. For now, documentation and support replies should describe the error plainly and avoid promising a stale-value fallback. The cache stores one entry per requested key, so expiry or an error for one key does not by itself clear the others.
changes: Clarified the expiry sequence and tightened repeated wording.

data.text: Come join our tiny reading club. Our unofficial rule is that nobody has to finish the book: every page, the first chapter, or just the description on the back is enough. Last month we spent half the evening on a chapter none of us liked, then stayed another hour because the conversation got good. We forgot to pick the next book before heading home and did it in the group chat the following morning, which is fairly typical. We meet around a kitchen table, share whatever snacks people bring, and follow a better question when one comes up. Bring a strong opinion, or listen for a while; both are welcome. We read what we can, say what we noticed, and enjoy having people to talk with about it. There is always room for another chair.
changes: Shaped the account into an invitation while keeping its informal details.
